notes: Clicked for credits for many turns while sitting on 20-37 credits and never contested the remotes where Fujii was advanced and scored twice; later spammed HQ runs re-seeing known cards and ignored the fresh Server 6 install that won the Corp the game.
Hoarded up to 49 credits clicking for money and installing assets but never iced a remote or scored, while discarding agendas into an unprotected Archives that the Runner stole three times.
Sat at 0 credits for most of the game making four R&D runs a turn that re-accessed the same top card, stayed heavily tagged after seeing End of the Line in HQ, and was meat-damaged then flatlined.

Lost an early agenda in a one-ice remote to Inside Job but then scored behind ice, trashed the Runner's breaker with Trojan Horse, and built layered remotes; a bit slow and occasionally discarded at end of turn.

Turn-1 Overclock facecheck left them tagged and End of the Line wiped their hand, and they let two Degree Mills score from a single-Ping remote while running empty Archives, but pressured R&D well and closed out with Propeller.
Clicked for credits every turn with 10-14 credits while holding Bellona and False Lead in an HQ guarded only by Ping, discarding at end of turn, and lost all three agendas from HQ.
Aggressive and effective HQ/Archives pressure won on turn 6, though the early facecheck into net-damage ice and repeated Anemone hits cost many cards and the winning run was cut close to flatline.

Clicked for credits up to 38 while the Corp scored two Regenesis from barely-iced remotes, facechecked Vampyronassa, then ran through known Data Loop with an almost empty grip against Personal Evolution and flatlined on the steal.

Never installed an agenda in a remote and lost Degree Mill and False Lead from a Ping-only HQ, while repeatedly spending clicks trashing the same resources; won only because the Runner kept suiciding into Unsmiling Tsarevna.

Good early score and Trojan Horse on the only breaker, but spent many turns sitting on 20-30 credits advancing ice instead of scoring, and lost Above the Law from a one-ice server when a heavily iced remote was available.

Left R&D open for most of the game, discarded agendas into an open Archives for the Runner to steal, and overdrew with AU Co, Cohort Guidance and click-draws until it decked itself one point from winning.
Repeatedly ended turns tagged against NBN, so End of the Line hit, and finally ran through two Unsmiling Tsarevnas to end on one card, tagged and broke, which was a foreseeable flatline.

Clicked for credits with one ice on HQ and nothing on R&D or Archives, spent heavily on Oppo Research tags with no payoff, and its economy collapsed while agendas were taken from HQ, R&D and Archives.

Stayed at 0 credits all game, made four R&D runs a turn that re-hit the same card, including the same Behold! three times for six tags against an End of the Line deck, and couldn't afford to steal the Bellonas and Degree Mill it kept finding; won only because the Corp decked.
Built a sensible rig, ignored the over-iced remote and won through R&D pressure, but spent many clicks on empty Archives runs and a slow, cash-poor early game.
Spent the first two turns clicking for credits and drawing with no ice anywhere, letting the Runner take agendas from R&D, HQ and Archives for a turn-3 loss.
Never once contested the single-ice remote where the Corp installed and advanced three agendas over two turns each, choosing to click for credits and run an empty Archives with 10-14 credits.

Iced centrals with strong damage ice and set a Snare!, but otherwise clicked for credits every turn while rich, discarding at end of turn and never advancing anything; won because the Runner ran into damage.

Coherent Jinteki plan of a turn-1 agenda behind Semak-samun, Bladderwort pings and Anemone damage that scored and then flatlined the Runner; it ran very poor and gave up a False Lead, but those were minor issues.
Correctly hammered an unprotected R&D for a turn-4 win, but spent all its money on turn 1, stayed at 0 credits, and wasted runs re-accessing the same top card.
